report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of vault.py: vault_rel validator, parse_frontmatter, read_page, discover_pages (partial). All claims in docstrings and comments are checked against visible code; several are uncheckable due to missing code.
risks: vault_rel | high | Symlink check walks the chain but does not handle symlink in vault_root itself. | Add symlink check for vault_root.resolve() chain.

vault_rel | medium | '..' segment check occurs before normalisation, but the docstring says it's to prevent 'a/../../b' normalising. However, the check rejects any '..' segment, so the stated reason is partially correct but the example is moot. | Clarify docstring or add normalisation test.
discover_pages | medium | The function is incomplete (ends mid-definition). Its behaviour cannot be verified. | Complete the function.
read_page | low | Path resolution uses vault_rel which does symlink check, but the docstring says 'never follows a symlink' which is accurate for the check. | No action needed.
todos: Consider adding a check for symlink in vault_root itself.

handoff.purpose: Defines vault and page data structures, vault_rel path validator, frontmatter parser, page reader, and partial page discovery.

claims.text: A folder of plain Markdown files. Deliberately Obsidian vault format
claims.why: The code does not enforce any Obsidian-specific structure beyond .md files and wikilinks are not mentioned in code.

claims.text: Vaults NEST: a global vault the operator owns, and one vault per project.
claims.why: No code implements nesting or distinguishes global vs project vaults beyond the Vault dataclass kind field.

claims.text: Every existing path parameter in web_api.py is an ID matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,160}$ — / is forbidden, so traversal is impossible by construction.
claims.why: web_api.py is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A wiki page rel MUST contain /.
claims.why: vault_rel does not require a '/' in rel; a single segment like 'note.md' is accepted.

claims.text: vault_rel is that guard, written before any endpoint exists so the endpoint cannot be written without it.
claims.why: No endpoint code is present; claim about order of writing is uncheckable.

claims.text: It is FAIL-CLOSED: every rejection returns None with a reason, and there is no 'best effort' path that resolves a suspicious spelling into something plausible.
claims.why: vault_rel returns (None, reason) for all refusal cases; no fallback resolution.

claims.text: absolute paths and drive letters -> escapes the vault outright
claims.why: vault_rel rejects paths starting with '/' or a drive letter pattern.

claims.text: any .. segment BEFORE resolution -> classic traversal; checked pre-resolve because a/../../b normalises to something innocent-looking
claims.why: vault_rel rejects any segment equal to '..' before any normalisation.

claims.text: a resolved path outside the vault -> the backstop, checked after resolve
claims.why: vault_rel checks resolved.relative_to(root_res) and returns reason if ValueError.

claims.text: symlinks anywhere on the chain -> a link inside the vault can point out
claims.why: vault_rel iterates over parts and checks is_symlink() on each intermediate path.

claims.text: : in a segment -> NTFS alternate data streams (page.md:$DATA writes a hidden fork)
Windows reserved device names -> CON, NUL, COM1 … open a device, not a file
claims.why: vault_rel checks stem (before extension) against _RESERVED set.

claims.text: trailing dots or spaces -> Windows silently strips them, so x.md. and x.md are the same file under a different name
claims.why: vault_rel checks seg != seg.rstrip('. ') and rejects if trailing dot or space.

claims.text: a suffix other than .md -> a vault holds prose, not executables
This module is READ-ONLY. It discovers, parses and validates; it never writes.
claims.why: No write operations (e.g., open for write, write_bytes) are present in this chunk.

claims.text: The write path needs its own gate list plus a Cerberus review, and it does not exist.
claims.why: No write path code is present; claim about non-existence is uncheckable but consistent.
read_page calls vault_rel which checks symlinks; size bounded by stat check.

claims.text: Refusals are RETURNED, not skipped — 'we could not read four pages' and 'there are no pages' must not look alike.
claims.why: The function is incomplete; the claim about returning refusals cannot be fully verified.

observations.what: vault_rel does not check for symlink in vault_root itself; only checks parts after root.
A wiki page rel MUST contain '/' claim is false; single segment paths are accepted.
discover_pages function is incomplete; ends mid-definition.
The docstring mentions 'Cerberus review' but no Cerberus usage is visible.
